subject: Dedicated capacity: rightsizing + expansion proposal for Quantico AI
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@quantico.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity - Q2 sizing question

Hi Dev / Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We reviewed our Q1 logs and wanted to get ahead of the renewal window. Attached is Q1 usage (usage_report_Q1.csv). A few highlights:
- Current committed pool: 64 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved in your Dedicated pool).
- Average utilization across workloads: ~58%; 95th percentile utilization by job: 78–84%.
- Tail latency spikes during product launches have been a problem (99th percentile latency up to 1.6s for generation requests).

We expect a 25–30% increase in inference volume in Q2 due to two new feature launches. We are evaluating two options: 1) increase committed GPUs by 25% (to ~80 GPUs) to keep headroom, or 2) keep current commit and rely on burst/autoscale but accept higher per-token costs.

Primary asks:
1) Can the Redwood team run a rightsizing analysis (capacity vs actual utilization) and model cost impact for both options?
2) If we expand commitments, what lead time is required to provision extra GPUs into our Dedicated pool and what are the billing/pricing implications?
3) Any recommendations to improve tail latency short-term (config tuning, cache, batching)?

We'd like to schedule a 30-min sync this week to review. I'm available Tue/Wed 10–2 PT.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, Quantico AI

-- attachment: usage_report_Q1.csv (CSV, 1.2 MB)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@quantico.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - Q2 sizing question

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the report and the clear ask. We're happy to run a rightsizing analysis and sketch cost/latency tradeoffs for both paths. Quick answers up-front:
• Lead time: for most cloud regions we can add capacity into a Dedicated pool within 2–5 business days once the commitment is finalized; for private/on-prem it's dependent on customer procurement.
• Billing: expansions can be added to the monthly committed capacity (pro-rated for the month) or handled as burst capacity at on-demand rates — we'll show both options.

Priyom — can you run a utilization simulation against Quantico's Q1 traces (they attached usage_report_Q1.csv) and produce: 1) a rightsized committed GPU recommendation for 95% of predicted Q2 load, 2) the percent change in token cost for the two options (commit vs burst), and 3) the expected 99th percentile latency impact assuming our standard batching/cache defaults?

I've attached a simple topology diagram (proposed_topology.png) that maps where additional GPUs would slot into their Dedicated pool and how we would route requests across model variants to mitigate tail spikes.

Hannah — are you OK with Tue 10:30 PT for a 30-min call? If not, Wed 11:00 PT also works.

Thanks,
Dev
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@quantico.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - Q2 sizing question

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the context. Commercially, we can support two paths:
1) Increase committed pool from 64 -> 80 GPUs. Estimated incremental commit: $X/month (see attached quote). We can apply a 10% renewal expansion credit if you sign the amendment before March 20.
2) Keep current commit and enable burst/autoscale to cover peaks. This minimizes upfront commitment but increases per-token spend during peak windows.

Attached is a draft quote (redwood-dedicated-quote.pdf) that shows both options and a modeled 12-month spend comparison using your Q1 data. If you want a firm PO path, we can generate an amendment document and parallel capacity provisioning once approved.

Diego — would you and Priyom be comfortable joining the call to walk through the topology and tradeoffs?

Hannah — confirming Tue 3/3 10:30 PT (Dev's slot shifted slightly to align). If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and the Deal (QL-7823) has been updated in HubSpot.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@quantico.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - Q2 sizing question

Hannah —

Thanks for the context and the meeting this morning — good to meet you. Follow-up notes and action items from our discussion: 

Summary of technical recommendation (short):
- Rightsize commit to 76 GPUs (midpoint between current and 25% expansion) to hit ~95% coverage for predicted Q2 load while avoiding large overcommitment.
- Update autoscaling policy: keep burst headroom at +15% to handle unexpected launches; implement pre-warming for scheduled release windows.
- Tail latency fixes (quick wins): enable aggressive KV prefix caching for stable request prefixes, reduce max batch latency from 100ms -> 60ms for lower 99th percentile latency, and enable mixed-precision quantization for the largest model family (saves ~18% GPU cycles).

Impact: these changes together shrink expected 99th percentile latency from 1.6s -> ~0.9–1.1s in our sim and reduce incremental GPU requirement versus naive expansion. We'll share the simulation artifacts.

Action items:
1) Priyom: post the utilization sim and a cost delta table for the two commercial options (commit -> 76 / 80 GPUs vs current + burst) by EOD Wed 3/4.
2) Dev/Marissa: confirm commercial path (amendment vs burst) and whether Quantico would like the 10% expansion credit (requires sign before 3/20).
3) Hannah: deliver any planned release dates for Q2 features so we can pre-warm and schedule canary windows.

I'll also forward the simulation logs and a short runbook for the pre-warm steps.
